title: Hs Linear Algebra Foundations — The Seven Components Doctrine
authority_level: FOUNDATIONAL — applies to all HUF, Hs, HCI-CNT, HCI-CNQ engines + plate generators + schemas. Any new engine or plate module shall name which of the seven components it employs and how.
parent_doctrine: huf-gov/HUF_GOVERNANCE_CHARTER.md Article V (Integrity of Purpose) + Article VI (Accountable Data) + Article VII (Accountable Resolution)

why_this_document_exists.trigger: Peter directive 2026-05-14 — 'peter, these are the main components that should be employed for hs: Symmetric Matrix · Property of Transpose · Matrix Decomposition · Eigen Vectors and Eigen Values · Strong Property of Symmetric Matrix · Spectral Decomposition · Visualization.'

doctrine_already_existed_implicitly: ILR-Helmert orthonormal basis (used in HCI/codawork2026/stage1_plates/ilr_triplet_plate.py and across Stage-1/2/3 plate generators) — relies on the Spectral Theorem for symmetric matrices
Variation matrix (computed implicitly in cnt.py) — symmetric matrix of var(log x_i/x_j)
Bearing tensor θ_ij (in cnt.py output `tensor.timesteps[*].bearing_tensor`) — antisymmetric matrix (θ_ji = -θ_ij)
Attractor fit (in cnq.py) — eigenvalue analysis of local Jacobian
κ^HS sensitivity vector (in cnt.py) — eigenvector-style direction on the simplex
Depth tower decomposition (in cnt.py output `depth_tower`) — recursive matrix decomposition into orthogonal components
Stage 2 CoDa-PCA biplot (in HCI/atlas/stage2_locked.py) — direct spectral decomposition of CLR covariance
the_past_that_was_checked.the_gap: The seven foundational linear-algebra components are employed throughout Hs but have never been named as a unified doctrine. New engine or plate-generator authors cannot consult a single document to know which foundations are load-bearing. External reviewers cannot easily verify that the Hs framework rests on standard mathematical foundations rather than ad-hoc constructions. The spectral-theorem justification of orthonormality is silent — the work uses it constantly but never cites it. This standard makes the foundations explicit.

why_this_document_exists.purpose: Names the seven linear-algebra components that every Hs engine and plate generator employs. Defines the contract: any new module declares which components it depends on and how. Establishes Stage-0 (Foundations Plate) as the visualization tier that surfaces the foundations directly — the same way Stage 1 surfaces bearings + CLR, Stage 2 surfaces helmsman + course, Stage 3 surfaces depth tower + IR + attractor.
why_this_document_exists.principle: Foundations are first-class. The framework rests on textbook linear algebra. Naming the seven components makes that visible to peers, future maintainers, and AI agents alike.

applies_to: All plate generators under HCI/codawork2026/, HCI/atlas/, and any future stage-* module
Schema documents: CNT_JSON_SCHEMA.md, CNQ_SCHEMA.md, and all derivative schemas
All Discovery Change Packets (DCPs) that introduce new computational modules
does_not_apply_to: Domain adapters (Order-0) — these are pre-engine and operate on raw data; foundations doctrine begins at the engine boundary
Conference-delivery formatting (PPTX, slide narrative, speaker notes) — these are downstream of standard outputs and need not name foundations explicitly
Repository admin JSONs (HS_ADMIN, HS_FAST_REFRESH, etc.) — these are bookkeeping, not computation

the_seven_components.name: Symmetric Matrix
the_seven_components.principle: A matrix M is symmetric iff M = M^T (i.e., M[i,j] = M[j,i] for all i, j). Symmetric matrices are the canonical objects of multivariate statistics because covariance and variation matrices are inherently symmetric.

where_it_lives_in_hs.variation_matrix: var(log x_i/x_j) computed implicitly inside cnt.py when forming pairwise log-ratios. Symmetric: var(log x_i/x_j) = var(log x_j/x_i). The variation matrix is the canonical CoDa second-order summary (Aitchison 1986).
where_it_lives_in_hs.clr_covariance: Cov(clr(X)) is symmetric and positive-semidefinite. Used in Stage 2 CoDa-PCA biplot construction.
where_it_lives_in_hs.gram_matrix_of_helmert_basis: H @ H^T = I (the (D-1)×(D-1) identity); H is the Helmert basis. This identity is the orthonormality certificate.
where_it_lives_in_hs.antisymmetric_sibling: The bearing tensor θ_ij is anti-symmetric: θ_ji = -θ_ij. Symmetric and antisymmetric matrices are duals; both are first-class in Hs.
files: HCI-CNT/engine/cnt.py — implicit in pairwise log-ratio computation

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: Variation matrix heatmap — D × D, colored by var(log x_i/x_j). Visual confirmation that M[i,j] = M[j,i].

the_seven_components.name: Property of Transpose
the_seven_components.principle: The transpose operation has algebraic properties that make linear-algebraic manipulation tractable: (A^T)^T = A, (A+B)^T = A^T + B^T, (AB)^T = B^T A^T, (A^{-1})^T = (A^T)^{-1}. For orthonormal matrices Q, Q^T = Q^{-1}, which is the property that makes coordinate changes lossless.
the_seven_components.mathematical_statement: For orthonormal Q: Q^T Q = Q Q^T = I, hence Q^T = Q^{-1}.

where_it_lives_in_hs.ilr_helmert_transform: ilr = clr @ H^T (project CLR onto ILR axes); clr = ilr @ H (project back). Both directions exact because H @ H^T = I. Implemented in ilr_triplet_plate.py line ~99 (clr_to_ilr function).
where_it_lives_in_hs.bearing_tensor_recovery: The pairwise bearing tensor is recovered from CLR coordinates via h_i - h_j, with the transpose relationship θ_ji = -θ_ij being a direct consequence.
where_it_lives_in_hs.covariance_propagation: Cov(M @ X) = M @ Cov(X) @ M^T — used implicitly when expressing CLR covariance in ILR coordinates.

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: Helmert basis H as heatmap (D-1 × D), overlaid with H @ H^T identity-check (should display perfect identity).

the_seven_components.name: Matrix Decomposition
the_seven_components.principle: A matrix decomposition factors a matrix M into a product of structurally-simpler matrices that reveal its essential properties. Common decompositions: LU, QR, Cholesky, SVD, Eigendecomposition. Each decomposition exposes a different facet of the matrix.
the_seven_components.mathematical_statement: M = ABC... where each factor has known structure (orthogonal, diagonal, triangular, etc.). The choice of decomposition reveals the relevant property.

where_it_lives_in_hs.closure_clr_ilr_chain: raw composition → closed composition (Aitchison closure) → CLR (centered log-ratio) → ILR (isometric log-ratio via Helmert basis). Each step is a decomposition of the original composition into a more analytically-tractable form.
where_it_lives_in_hs.bearing_tensor_pairwise_decomposition: The trajectory at each timestep decomposes into D(D-1)/2 pairwise bearings — an antisymmetric-matrix decomposition emitted in cnt.py as tensor.timesteps[t].bearing_tensor.
where_it_lives_in_hs.depth_tower_decomposition: cnt.py output `depth_tower` decomposes the time series into nested orthogonal subspaces — Order-3 in the Output Doctrine.
where_it_lives_in_hs.stage_2_codapca: CoDa-PCA biplot performs eigendecomposition of CLR covariance → orthogonal principal components ordered by variance.
files: HCI-CNT/engine/cnt.py — multiple decompositions emitted to canonical JSON
HCI/codawork2026/stage1_plates/stage1_plates_raw.py — Section Plate visualizes the pairwise decomposition
HCI/codawork2026/stage1_plates/ilr_triplet_plate.py — Triplet Plate visualizes the ILR decomposition

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: Composition decomposition tree — raw → closed → CLR → ILR, with each arrow labeled by the operation and visualized as a small heatmap or scatter.

the_seven_components.name: Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues
the_seven_components.principle: For a square matrix M, an eigenvector v is a non-zero vector that M scales rather than rotates: M v = λ v, where λ is the eigenvalue. Eigenvectors are the privileged directions of M; eigenvalues are how strongly M acts in those directions.
the_seven_components.mathematical_statement: M v = λ v, v ≠ 0. Real n×n matrices have at most n eigenvalues (with multiplicity).

where_it_lives_in_hs.attractor_fit: cnq.py computes the eigenvalues of the local linearization to fit an exponentially-contracting attractor (output: amplitude A + contraction λ + period). Visible in CNQ dashboard's diagnostics box as `attractor_fit.amplitude_A` and `attractor_fit.contraction_lambda`.
where_it_lives_in_hs.kappa_hs_sensitivity: κ^HS in cnt.py is the eigenvector-style sensitivity direction of the navigation tensor — names which carrier is most responsible for trajectory change.
where_it_lives_in_hs.coda_pca_axes: Stage 2 CoDa-PCA biplot uses eigendecomposition of Cov(clr(X)) to find principal axes.

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: Eigenvalue scree plot — eigenvalues of CLR covariance in descending order. Cumulative variance-explained curve. Visual signature of dimension reduction potential.

the_seven_components.name: Strong Property of Symmetric Matrices (Spectral Theorem)
the_seven_components.principle: Every real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors. This is the Spectral Theorem and is the strongest single result in elementary linear algebra. It guarantees that symmetric matrices can ALWAYS be diagonalized by an orthogonal change of basis.
the_seven_components.mathematical_statement: If M = M^T (real), then there exist orthonormal Q (Q^T Q = I) and diagonal Λ such that M = Q Λ Q^T. All eigenvalues of M are real.

where_it_lives_in_hs.silent_justification_of_ilr: ILR balances form an orthonormal basis of the simplex's tangent space precisely because the Helmert (or any sequential-binary-partition) construction relies on the Spectral Theorem. Without the Spectral Theorem, ILR coordinates would not be guaranteed orthonormal.
where_it_lives_in_hs.silent_justification_of_codapca: CoDa-PCA produces real principal axes with real variance because Cov(clr(X)) is symmetric. Spectral Theorem.
where_it_lives_in_hs.silent_justification_of_attractor_fit: The local Jacobian, when symmetrizable, has real eigenvalues that name expansion vs contraction unambiguously.
where_it_lives_in_hs.the_gap: Until HUF-STD-003, this load-bearing theorem was never cited in any Hs document. The work used it constantly but did not name it. Stage-0 plates surface this dependency explicitly.
files: ALL of the above are downstream of the Spectral Theorem. There is no single file that 'computes' the theorem — it justifies the whole construction.

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: Verification panel — compute Σ = Q Λ Q^T for the CLR covariance, display ||Σ - Q Λ Q^T|| as a numeric norm at the IEEE floor. Visual proof that the theorem holds at machine precision on the data.

the_seven_components.name: Spectral Decomposition
the_seven_components.principle: The explicit factorization M = Q Λ Q^T for symmetric M (or M = U Σ V^T for general M, SVD). The eigenvalues on the diagonal Λ rank-order the importance of each direction; truncating Λ at rank k produces the optimal rank-k approximation (Eckart–Young theorem).
the_seven_components.mathematical_statement: Σ = Q Λ Q^T, where Λ = diag(λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ ... ≥ λ_n). Rank-k truncation: Σ_k = Σ_{i=1}^k λ_i q_i q_i^T.

where_it_lives_in_hs.coda_pca: Stage 2 CoDa-PCA is direct spectral decomposition of CLR covariance. Plots the first 2 or 3 principal components on a biplot.
where_it_lives_in_hs.implicit_in_attractor_fit: cnq.py attractor_fit performs spectral analysis of the local linearization.
where_it_lives_in_hs.rank_k_reconstruction: Could be added — compute Σ_k for k = 1, 2, 3 and report cumulative variance.
where_it_lives_in_hs.the_gap: There is no dedicated plate that shows the full spectral decomposition Q Λ Q^T side-by-side. CoDa-PCA shows the first two eigenvectors as biplot axes; it does not show all D-1 eigenvectors, the eigenvalue spectrum, or the rank-k reconstruction explicitly. Stage-0 closes this gap.

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: Two-panel plate: (a) eigenvalue spectrum bar chart with cumulative-explained-variance overlay; (b) orthonormal eigenbasis Q visualized as a heatmap of (D-1) × (D-1) — each column an eigenvector — with carrier labels on rows.

the_seven_components.name: Visualization
the_seven_components.principle: Linear algebra without visualization is opaque. Every component above admits a visual representation: symmetric matrix as heatmap, transpose as axis swap, decomposition as factorized panels, eigenvectors as arrows, eigenvalues as a scree plot, spectral decomposition as a reconstruction-quality curve. The Stage-0 Foundations Plate is the visual surface that makes the foundations legible.
the_seven_components.mathematical_statement: Visualization is not a mathematical statement; it is a pedagogical and verification requirement. A plate suite that visualizes components 1–6 is the deliverable.

where_it_lives_in_hs.section_plate: Stage 1 Section Plate visualizes pairwise bearings (antisymmetric matrix consequence) + CLR coordinates (decomposition consequence).
where_it_lives_in_hs.triplet_plate: Stage 1 Triplet Plate visualizes ILR-Helmert orthonormal basis (Spectral Theorem consequence) as three orthogonal scatter projections.
where_it_lives_in_hs.stage_2_plates: Stage 2 plates include CoDa-PCA biplot (eigenvector consequence).
where_it_lives_in_hs.stage_3_plates: Stage 3 plates show depth tower (recursive decomposition consequence) and attractor fit (eigenvalue consequence).
where_it_lives_in_hs.cnq_dashboard: CNQ dashboard shows Hs(t), ω(t), K_eff + TV, helmsman σ(t), spike detector — all consequences of the foundations, none of them surfacing the foundations themselves.
where_it_lives_in_hs.the_gap_stage_0: No existing plate surfaces foundations 1–6 directly. Stage-0 Foundations Plate (HCI/codawork2026/stage0_foundations/) closes this gap.

the_seven_components.stage_0_visualization: The Stage-0 Foundations Plate IS this component. See HCI/codawork2026/stage0_foundations/foundations_plate.py.

for_engine_authors: Every new computational module shall declare which of the seven components it employs in its docstring.
Every output JSON block whose computation depends on a foundation shall name the dependency in the schema doc.
Spectral Theorem invocations (any orthonormal-basis or eigendecomposition step) shall cite HUF-STD-003 component 5.
for_plate_authors: Every new plate generator shall declare in its docstring which foundations its visualization rests on.
Stage-0 plates are reserved for direct visualization of foundations 1–6; Stage-N plates (N ≥ 1) visualize derived quantities.
Stage-0 plates produce PDF / PNG / SVG per HUF-STD-002 link 4.
for_schema_authors: JSON output blocks that record eigenstructures (eigenvalues, eigenvectors, principal components, contraction rates) shall be tagged with foundation reference HUF-STD-003-§4 or HUF-STD-003-§6.
Symmetric-matrix outputs (variation matrices, covariances) shall be tagged HUF-STD-003-§1.
Orthonormal-basis outputs (ILR coordinates, Helmert basis matrices) shall be tagged HUF-STD-003-§5.
conformance_requirements.verification: The consistency checker (scripts/check_ai_refresh_consistency.py) shall include a CHK-FOUNDATIONS-001 rule (post-conference) that audits docstring declarations against module computational content.

the_maxim: Foundations are first-class. Symmetric matrices have orthonormal eigenbases. Transposes invert orthonormal matrices. Decompositions reveal structure. Eigenvectors name the privileged directions. The Spectral Theorem is the silent justification. Spectral decomposition is the visible factorization. Visualization makes all six legible. The instrument reads. The expert decides. The hashes carry the receipts. The vocabulary holds the line. The foundations carry the bedrock.
